## Household and background

Harold Vance (born June 15, 1968 — 57 at year end) is single with no dependents and lives at 9 Overlook Terrace in Anytown. He has worked all year at Kestrel Valley Machine Works — one W-2, box 1 wages $39,674.00, box 2 federal withholding $7,274.00.

Like the rest of the company he was on the self-only high-deductible health plan (HDHP) through June 30; on July 1 the employer switched everyone to a low-deductible PPO that is not HSA-eligible, so his HDHP coverage ran exactly six months. His employer seeded $260.00 into the HSA in the spring (W-2 box 12, code W). Being over 55 and wanting to catch up before retirement, he contributed aggressively himself: $2,000.00 through the year, plus another $100.00 in March 2026 that he designated for tax year 2025. He took nothing out of the account.

## Interview

**Q.** Which months of 2025 were you covered by the high-deductible plan?

**A.** January through June — the plan change hit everyone on July 1.

**Q.** On December 1, 2025, were you covered by an HDHP?

**A.** No — the replacement PPO isn't a high-deductible plan.

**Q.** Was the HDHP self-only or family coverage?

**A.** Self-only — it's just me.

**Q.** You turned 57 this year — were you 55 or older by December 31?

**A.** Yes, 57 in June. That's exactly why I pushed the contributions — the catch-up room.

**Q.** Besides the $260 your employer put in, how much did you contribute yourself?

**A.** $2,000 during the year, and $100 more in March 2026 that I told the custodian to count toward 2025 — $2,100 all told.

**Q.** Did you take any money out of the HSA in 2025?

**A.** No — it's all staying in for retirement.

**Q.** Were you enrolled in Medicare, covered under anyone else's health plan, or claimable as a dependent on someone else's return?

**A.** No to all three.

## Preparer notes

- Not an eligible individual on December 1 → no §223(b)(8) last-month rule; age 55+ folds the $1,000 catch-up into the proration base: ($4,300 + $1,000) x 6/12 = line-3 limit $2,650 (vs $2,150 under 55).
- Line 11 room = $2,650 − $260 employer = $2,390; HSA deduction (line 13) = min($2,100 own contributions, $2,390) = $2,100 → Schedule 1 line 13. The catch-up is load-bearing: an under-55 filer would be capped at $1,890.
- Total contributions $2,360 stay under the $2,650 limit — no excess. No distributions, so Form 8889 Part II is empty.
